title: HB554 (2018 Regular): AN ACT relating to school safety and declaring an emergency.

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, Kentucky); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Kentucky text (Draft, 0000-00-00; official copy, https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/recorddocuments/bill/18RS/HB554/bill.pdf (LegiScan doc 1744387))
provenance.note: Draft print (18 RS BR 1853); no passage vote. Section 3 text shown after the bill: "Any other persons, including, but not limited to" is struck and the team member wording is added. Rest of Section 2 (course hours, screening, fees) and the liability protections not quoted.

operative_text:
Section 1 (new section of KRS Chapter 158): (2) Beginning July 1, 2018, for each school that does not have a dedicated full-time school resource officer or a school security officer, a local board of education shall approve an emergency response team. Members of the emergency response team shall be authorized to carry a firearm under Section 3 of this Act.
Section 1 (new section of KRS Chapter 158): (4) Each member of a school's emergency response team shall: (a) Be selected as a member by the school district; (b) Be a full-time employee of the school district; (c) Hold a valid license to carry a concealed deadly weapon under KRS 237.110; and (d) Hold a school safety certification received under Section 2 of this Act.
Section 1 (new section of KRS Chapter 158): (7) A member of the emergency response team shall be responsible for the purchase of the firearm, ammunition, and any other associated costs. A member shall not be compensated for the purchases made pursuant to his or her appointment or during service as a member, except that a local board of education may provide payment to a member of any reasonable and necessary expenses incurred relating to obtaining school safety certification.
Section 2 (new section of KRS Chapter 16): (1) The Department of Kentucky State Police shall establish a process to enable qualified firearms instructors certified under KRS 237.122 to obtain an additional certification in school safety training.
Section 3 (KRS 527.070): (f) Members of a public school's emergency response team under Section 1 of this Act, exhibitors of historical displays, or any other persons who have been authorized to carry a firearm pursuant to the written policies or written authorization of the board of education or board of trustees of the public or private institution;
